asset_name: SING IMT(TM) System, model NG SI IMT 3X
mechanism: SING IMT is a monocular, implantable miniature Galilean telescope/visual prosthetic device. When implanted during cataract surgery, its micro-optics work with the cornea to create a telephoto system that magnifies straight-ahead images about 2.7x and projects them onto healthier retina surrounding the degenerated macula, while the fellow eye provides peripheral vision.
phase: Not applicable; implantable ophthalmic device study
development_status: NCT04796545 is a recruiting, prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm post-market clinical follow-up study in 76 adults age 55 years or older with central vision impairment from end-stage AMD. ClinicalTrials.gov lists the assigned intervention as a device, with actual start on 2022-09-13, estimated primary completion in 2027-02, estimated study completion in 2028-12, and no posted results. HRA describes the same PMCF study as evaluating a CE-marked SING IMT System, model NG SI IMT 3X. A separate U.S. CONCERTO study, NCT05438732, is recruiting under FDA-regulated device status and has estimated completion in 2025-12.
expected_launch_window: Not applicable to drug pipeline launch; CE-marked post-market device in Europe and investigational/not FDA-approved for SING IMT in the United States
expected_launch_date: EU CE mark in 2020; U.S. FDA approval date not available
clinical_summary: The assigned PMCF study is designed to evaluate SING IMT safety by 12-month endothelial cell density loss, with secondary endpoints for incision size, surgical complications, best-corrected visual acuity, and surgeon usability. Company and HRA sources position SING IMT as a CE-marked implant for late-stage AMD patients who lack restorative treatment options beyond low-vision aids. A 35-patient Italian retrospective cohort published in Heliyon reported 6-month distance and near vision gains after SING IMT implantation, including at least 2-line BCDVA gain in 68.6% of operated eyes and near-reading ability increasing from 28.6% at baseline to 97.1%. Evidence remains limited by small, non-randomized cohorts and no posted results from the assigned PMCF or U.S. CONCERTO trial.
safety_summary: NCT04796545's primary endpoint is percent decrease in endothelial cell density at 12 months, and the study monitors surgical complications, adverse events, serious adverse events, device stability, anterior chamber depth, and medication use. Published 6-month SING IMT data reported mean ECD change of -280.7 cells/mm2 (-11.4%) and corneal edema as the most frequent adverse event, with cases resolved using topical medications. Company and FDA analog materials warn that IMT/SING IMT surgery can involve inflammatory deposits or precipitates, increased intraocular pressure, corneal edema, vision-impairing corneal edema, corneal transplant, decreased visual acuity, worse vision rather than improvement, peripheral-field restriction in the implanted eye, and required postoperative rehabilitation; driving is contraindicated with SING IMT.
management_tools: Exclude from drug/pharma pipeline launch dashboards unless implantable ophthalmic devices are in scope

Medical-benefit prior authorization requiring end-stage bilateral AMD, geographic atrophy or disciform scar with foveal involvement, qualifying visual acuity, cataract status, no active CNV, adequate fellow-eye peripheral vision, and external telescope simulator response
Coverage limited to monocular implantation by trained/qualified ophthalmic surgeons with documentation of informed consent and acceptance of surgical/rehabilitation requirements
Site-of-care and billing-code controls for CPT 0308T and HCPCS C1840, including packaged device payment review under OPPS/ASC rules
Postoperative low-vision rehabilitation and continuation documentation rather than pharmacy refill controls
Evidence review trigger when NCT04796545 PMCF or NCT05438732 CONCERTO results post or when FDA acts on the SING IMT PMA supplement
evidence_gaps: No results are posted for NCT04796545, and the primary completion date is estimated for 2027-02.
NCT05438732 CONCERTO is the more direct U.S. FDA-regulated device study, but no ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted there either.
No direct U.S. SING IMT device price was found; cost estimates use 2026 CMS procedure payment analogs for ocular telescope implantation.
European CE-marked availability and global implantation claims do not establish U.S. FDA approval or U.S. launch timing for SING IMT.
Published SING IMT outcome evidence is currently small, retrospective, and short-term relative to the 12-month PMCF endpoints and long-term corneal safety concerns.

expected_launch_window.value: Not applicable to drug pipeline launch; CE-marked post-market device in Europe and investigational/not FDA-approved for SING IMT in the United States
expected_launch_window.method: Classified the assigned record from ClinicalTrials.gov intervention type, HRA CE-mark/post-market context, and company statements on CE mark and U.S. FDA status instead of applying a drug launch forecast.
expected_launch_window.explanation: NCT04796545 is not a drug pipeline asset; it is a post-market clinical follow-up study of a CE-marked implantable ophthalmic device. A separate U.S. PMA supplemental study is recruiting, and no SING IMT FDA approval date was found.

annual_cost_range.method: Used April 2026 CMS procedure payment analogs because no direct SING IMT price was found. Low equals ASC CPT 0308T payment of $12,196.25, rounded to $12,196. High equals hospital outpatient OPPS CPT 0308T payment of $16,817.36, rounded to $16,817; HCPCS C1840 is packaged/no separate payment in the CMS sources.
annual_cost_range.explanation: This is a first-year, one-time procedure payment proxy, not recurring annual drug cost. It excludes payer-specific contracts, geographic wage adjustment, surgeon professional payment, preoperative screening, rehabilitation visits, complications, follow-up care, and European private-market pricing.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted device mechanism, lack of restorative options for end-stage AMD, post-market CE use, published short-term SING IMT visual gains, and prior first-generation IMT analog evidence against small non-randomized evidence and no posted PMCF/CONCERTO results.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: For eligible end-stage AMD patients, an implanted telescope that improves central visual function can be clinically meaningful. Confidence is moderated because the assigned study has no results and available SING IMT outcomes are short-term and limited.

budget_impact.method: Assessed one-time procedure payment around $12,000-$17,000, narrow end-stage AMD eligibility, medical-benefit controls, surgeon/site requirements, and lack of broad pharmacy utilization.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient episode cost is material, but uptake should be constrained by strict patient selection, surgical capacity, low-vision rehabilitation requirements, and U.S. investigational status for SING IMT.

disruption_risk.method: Rated operational disruption from implantable-device authorization, procedure/site billing, rehabilitation workflow, evidence monitoring, and possible future U.S. FDA activity rather than pharmacy formulary disruption.
disruption_risk.explanation: The device could require medical-policy updates if U.S. approval is pursued, but it should not materially disrupt drug formulary operations. Current disruption is mainly medical-benefit, surgical-network, and evidence-review work.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to device exclusion concern, CE-marked post-market status, U.S. investigational status, no posted pivotal/PMCF results, and existing medical-benefit management pathways.
recommended_action.explanation: Do not treat this as a drug pipeline launch. Track NCT04796545 and NCT05438732 results, FDA PMA supplement activity, CE/post-market safety evidence, coding/payment updates, and payer medical-policy changes.

quality_flags: Exclusion concern: SING IMT is an implantable ophthalmic visual-prosthesis device, not a drug or biologic pipeline asset.
The assigned NCT04796545 record is a post-market clinical follow-up study of a CE-marked device, so it should not be modeled as a future drug launch.
Company sources state SING IMT is not currently FDA approved in the United States; the related U.S. CONCERTO study NCT05438732 is FDA-regulated as a device study and remains without posted results.

ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT04796545 as not FDA-regulated as a drug and not FDA-regulated as a device, consistent with non-U.S. post-market context; this should not be interpreted as U.S. device approval.
No direct SING IMT price was found; the cost range uses 2026 CMS ocular telescope procedure payment analogs and represents a one-time first-year episode proxy rather than recurring annual drug spend.
Evidence maturity concern: no results are posted for NCT04796545, and published SING IMT outcomes are short-term, small, and non-randomized.
Safety/operations concern: device implantation requires surgery, strict ocular selection criteria, endothelial cell monitoring, adverse-event management, and postoperative low-vision rehabilitation.
